title: 2026-06-17-midyear-inference-governance-scale-readout
next_steps: Redwood to share revised pricing sheet for Dedicated with burst options
SE to run 24-hour throughput benchmark with Peregrine subset of traffic (50k daily requests)
Security to send SOC2/ISO artifacts and KMS integration note
Schedule follow-up deep-dive on canary rollout policy week of 2026-06-28
action_items: Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE): run throughput benchmark using Peregrine prompt set by 2026-06-22
Maya Patel (AE): update Dedicated pricing model and email proposal by 2026-06-19
Priya Singh (Customer): share current SSO/SAML metadata and HSM usage constraints by 2026-06-21
Marcus Tan (Customer): provide sample token distribution and tail-latency SLOs by 2026-06-20
summary: Mid-year checkpoint focusing on governance, scaling plan for Dedicated capacity, cost tradeoffs, and security artifacts. Customer is interested in a hybrid approach: Dedicated for peak traffic with hosted fallback during bursts. Key asks: 24-hour benchmark, explicit pricing with burst/overage terms, and confirmation of KMS/HSM flow in Private deployments.
questions: Can Redwood guarantee sub-120ms median generation for our 512-token baseline?
How does KV cache hit-rate affect billing and latency in steady-state?
What's the expected RPO/RTO for Private on-prem control plane?
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll kick off in a minute. Meeting is scheduled for 1 hour but we've got a few extra if needed. Lara, you got the agenda?
[00:30] Lara (Peregrine): Yep, thanks Maya. High level today, usage review, cost options for Dedicated, security items, and then we want a plan for scaling into Q4.
[01:00] Diego (Redwood SE): Cool, I'll present the throughput data and then we can talk about the batching/kv cache stuff. Quick note, some of the numbers I pulled are from our canary runs so there may be variance.
[01:45] Marcus (Peregrine): Sounds good. We're most concerned about tail latency rather than median — we can't have spikes during checkout flows.
[02:30] Priya (Peregrine): Also from security: KMS/HSM is non-negotiable for us, we need an HSM-backed key provenance and audit logs.
[03:15] Diego (Redwood SE): Understood. On Private we support customer-managed KMS and integrations with HSMs, and audit logs are available — though the on-prem package has a slightly different audit retention by default. I'll get the exact retention numbers after the call.
[04:00] Maya (Redwood AE): To frame costs: Peregrine's current monthly token footprint would sit in our mid-tier Dedicated band, but your burst pattern — that sharp weekend spike — is why a hybrid config might be best. You can reserve baseline capacity and rely on hosted fallback.
[05:00] Ethan (Peregrine): Quick clarification, if we use reserved Dedicated with hosted fallback, how's data residency handled for the fallback? We can't have certain PII leave region.
[05:45] Jordan (Redwood CSM): Good question. Fallback can be constrained by routing policy — you can set region-only fallback or disable fallback for endpoints flagged as sensitive. We'll share the routing policy doc.
[06:30] Marcus (Peregrine): Ok — show me the numbers.
[07:00] Diego (Redwood SE): (screen share) Here's a 72-hour run we did with your typical prompt mix. Median for 512 token baseline was ~95ms on A100-style nodes, p95 was 310ms when we forced a naive batching config. When we enable continuous batching and prefix KV caching — which in our logs was labeled KV cash in one export haha — p95 drops to 180–200ms. Note: the KV hit-rate on your dataset was about 38% in this run.
[08:00] Lara (Peregrine): 38% KV hit-rate... is that tunable? Can we prewarm common prefixes?
[08:30] Diego (Redwood SE): Yes, cache warming and some prompt unification helps. Also quantization profile affects memory and throughput. For Peregrine's mix we saw no quality regression at int8-qat for most assistant flows.
[09:00] Priya (Peregrine): Does quantization affect our compliance posture? Like, can we still do customer-managed encryption?
[09:45] Maya (Redwood AE): Yes, quantization is purely a runtime model optimization and doesn't change encryption-at-rest or key management. The model binaries are stored encrypted under your KMS keys in Private deployments.
[10:30] Marcus (Peregrine): Walk me through failure modes. If Dedicated pool gets saturated, what's the fallback sequence?
[11:00] Diego (Redwood SE): Policy-based routing. First try Dedicated pool, then identical model variant on hosted, then a lower-cost quantized variant if configured. You can set per-route fallbacks and canary percentages. We also support automatic throttling to preserve SLOs.
[12:00] Lara (Peregrine): But what about fidelity — we can't have a version that returns wildly different behavior during fallback.
[12:40] Diego (Redwood SE): Right — that's why we recommend model pinning and a rollback policy. You can pin versions and only allow fallback to vetted variants. We can also run a model delta eval against your prompt set to quantify expected drift.
[13:30] Priya (Peregrine): We'll need the eval harness and the dataset privacy terms.
[14:15] Maya (Redwood AE): We'll include a sample eval harness and instructions; note that for Private/on-prem deployments you control the eval data.
[15:00] Marcus (Peregrine): Pricing — show us the Dedicated cost with burst.
[15:45] Maya (Redwood AE): Sure. Baseline reserved is X per month for the capacity you need. Burst is priced as a per-hour additive plus an overage per token if you exceed burst capacity. I'll follow up with a spreadsheet that models your weekend spikes.
[16:30] Lara (Peregrine): We're sensitive to unit economics. If we move more to caching and batching, what kind of cost delta do we see?
[17:00] Diego (Redwood SE): In our bench, enabling prefix caching and 64-request batching reduced token-supply CPU time by ~28%, roughly translating to 18–22% cost reduction after amortizing latency-sensitive reservations. Your mileage will vary based on repeatability of prompts.
[18:00] Ethan (Peregrine): Any limitations on private/VPC networking? We have strict egress rules.
[18:45] Jordan (Redwood CSM): Private deployments run in your VPC and we can coordinate peering or a transit gateway. We'll share the network runbook. For fully air-gapped installs there's an extra lead time.
[19:30] Priya (Peregrine): About the SOC2 docs — can you provide the type 2 report and the control mappings?
[20:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Yes, security will share SOC2 type 2 and ISO artifact links. Note some artifacts are redacted for customer safety but we'll provide control mappings.
[21:00] Marcus (Peregrine): Ok — the benchmark. We want a 24-hour run with our traffic shape and to see token counts, latency distributions, and failure rates.
[21:45] Diego (Redwood SE): We'll need the sample prompt set and a hashed token distribution. Marcus, can you send that?
[22:30] Marcus (Peregrine): Yes, I can export and share a scrubbed distribution. ETA 6/20.
[23:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Great. On SLAs — Dedicated comes with uptime and latency SLOs. We'll attach the SLA doc in the follow up.
[23:45] Lara (Peregrine): A couple more items — can we get more detail on the canary rollout options? We want linear ramp vs. time-based ramp config examples.
[24:30] Diego (Redwood SE): We support percent-based canaries, time-based windows, and traffic-shape based triggers. We'll send examples and a recommended policy for low-risk model swaps.
[25:15] Priya (Peregrine): Also, from a governance perspective we need RBAC differentiation between model admins and app owners.
[26:00] Jordan (Redwood CSM): RBAC is role based; you can create roles with restricted deploy and rollback permissions. We'll include a sample RBAC matrix.
[27:00] Lara (Peregrine): Any competitors doing this better?
[27:45] Maya (Redwood AE): Some larger clouds offer endpoint autoscaling but not the same batching/kv cache optimizations off-the-shelf. Anthropic and AWS Bedrock came up in our RFP competitors — bedrock has single-provider lock-in concerns.
[28:30] Marcus (Peregrine): Noted. For the benchmark run, can you also surface per-token cost modeling for both dedicated + hosted fallback vs hosted-only?
[29:15] Diego (Redwood SE): Yes, that's part of the benchmark output. We'll produce a spreadsheet with cost per 1M tokens under both scenarios and run sensitivity for KV hit-rate 20–60%.
[30:00] Priya (Peregrine): Can we get an RTO/RPO figure for the Private control plane? If updates fail or the control plane is out, what's the impact?
[30:45] Diego (Redwood SE): RTO for control plane is typically 30–60 minutes depending on the setup; for on-prem full air-gapped installs it's longer. Runtime inference continues for already-provisioned nodes but orchestrated rollouts will be impacted. We'll capture exact figures for your topology.
[32:00] Lara (Peregrine): Good. Onboarding timeline — we want pilot in July, full roll by October. Feasible?
[32:45] Maya (Redwood AE): Yes, with the benchmark and security review completed in two weeks a July pilot looks possible. We'll work backwards on milestones.
[34:00] Marcus (Peregrine): One more technical — how do you handle KV cache invalidation when model weights update?
[34:45] Diego (Redwood SE): Cache invalidation is versioned — when a model variant is rolled, existing KV namespaces can be invalidated or warmed in parallel. There's an API to control that and we can run a warm-up job.
[36:00] Priya (Peregrine): Do you log prompt text in the control plane? We need redaction or tokenization for audit.
[36:45] Jordan (Redwood CSM): By default we do not persist raw prompts for customers on Private; for hosted we offer redaction and scrubbing policies. We'll document the default retention and redaction knobs.
[38:00] Lara (Peregrine): Ok let's do a quick recap and next steps.
[38:30] Maya (Redwood AE): Recap: Redwood will run a 24-hour benchmark with Peregrine's prompt set, provide pricing sheet with dedicated+burst modeling, send SOC2/ISO and KMS/HSM notes, and share routing policy and RBAC examples. Customer will provide scrubbed token distribution, SAML metadata, and SLO targets.
[39:30] Marcus (Peregrine): I'll get the token distribution and SLOs by 6/20.
[40:00] Priya (Peregrine): I'll send SSO metadata and HSM constraints by 6/21.
[40:30] Maya (Redwood AE): We'll circulate the proposal and schedule the canary deep-dive week of 6/28.
[41:00] Diego (Redwood SE): Action item: I'll queue the throughput job and will share results into the repo. Expect the first pass by 6/22.
[41:45] Lara (Peregrine): Couple of small items — can we get a sample rollback runbook?
[42:30] Jordan (Redwood CSM): Yes, we have a runbook and a template for rollback and incident comms.
[43:00] Ethan (Peregrine): One thing — we noticed an odd token-count anomaly in one of the Redwood SDK exports where 'KV' was printed as 'K-V cash', hope it's not important but just flagging transcription quirks.
[43:45] Diego (Redwood SE): (laughs) we've seen worse in logs. We'll verify the export pipeline.
[45:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Anything else?
[45:30] Lara (Peregrine): No, that's it from product. Thanks all.
[46:00] Marcus (Peregrine): Thanks, appreciate the detail.
[46:30] Priya (Peregrine): Thanks.
[47:00] Maya (Redwood AE): End note — we'll mark the follow-up items in the CRM and share meeting notes within 24 hours.
[61:00] (meeting ends)
